title: When being an "expert" is harmful: why assuming you know your market blocks learning
summary: Jason Cohen argues that expertise makes founders skip customer conversations and miss what has changed. A founder certain about pricing learned more in one week of quick vendor calls than in a year. Use experience for hypotheses, not decisions, and test every assumption with real customers.

principles.text: Learning happens when an assumption gets kicked out from under you, so go test the ones you're surest about.
principles.quote: whenever an assumption is kicked out from under you, that's when you learn the most.
